title: SLPO: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoners That Think in Vectors
hook: Latent reasoners think in continuous vectors, not tokens — but couldn't learn from outcome rewards the way chain-of-thought models can. SLPO gives them a surrogate policy so RL finally works.
key_points: RL with verifiable rewards is the standard recipe for test-time scaling in explicit chain-of-thought reasoners, but decoding every step as a token is costly.
Latent reasoning carries intermediate computation as continuous vectors and can match explicit CoT at far shorter horizons.
But latent reasoners stay imitation-bound: their trajectories lack a tractable per-step likelihood and an adaptive stopping signal, so outcome rewards can't guide them.
SLPO adds an empirical surrogate policy density over latent transitions, giving trajectory-level credit assignment.
A correctness-supervised stopping head, refined by outcome-reward optimization, becomes a variable-horizon policy — spending more latent compute on harder problems.
content_html: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is now the standard way to unlock test-time scaling in reasoning models — but only for explicit chain-of-thought, where every intermediate step is decoded as a language token. That's expensive. Runyang You, Zhiyuan Liu, Yongqi Li, and Wenjie Li target a cheaper alternative: latent reasoning, which carries intermediate computation as continuous vectors and can match explicit CoT at far shorter horizons.
extra_html:
The gap

The catch is that latent reasoners have stayed imitation-bound — trained to copy, not to improve from outcome rewards the way explicit CoT already has. Two things block outcome-reward RL: a latent trajectory has no tractable per-step likelihood to assign credit against, and no adaptive stopping interface to decide when the model is done thinking under a fixed budget.

What SLPO adds

Surrogate Latent Policy Optimization tackles both. It fits an empirical surrogate policy density over latent transitions, giving a trajectory-level signal RL can optimize, and it adds a correctness-supervised stopping head that outcome-reward optimization sharpens into a variable-horizon policy. Across continuous and soft "thinking" settings, the authors report SLPO improving Pass@k under parallel sampling and allocating longer latent computation to harder instances, with higher deterministic accuracy. See the arXiv paper for the method and results.

related.title: Chain of Thought Is a Scaling Trap? The Case for Latent Reasoning
related.hook: A visible chain of thought reads like the model's thinking — but it can be an unfaithful, expensive trace. The next wave reasons in hidden state instead of tokens.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
related.hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.

flashcards.prompt: Why couldn't outcome-reward RL be applied to latent reasoners before SLPO?
flashcards.back_html: Latent trajectories lack a tractable per-step likelihood and an adaptive stopping interface under a fixed thinking budget, so outcome rewards had nothing to attach credit to.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'latent reasoning' carry intermediate computation as, instead of language tokens?

choices.text: Continuous vectors in the model's hidden state
Extra rows appended to the training dataset
Discrete symbols from a separate vocabulary

flashcards.explanation_html: Latent reasoning keeps intermediate steps as continuous vectors rather than decoding each one as a token, which lets it match CoT at shorter horizons.

flashcards.prompt: What role does SLPO's correctness-supervised stopping head play?

choices.text: Outcome-reward optimization refines it into a variable-horizon policy that spends more latent compute on harder problems
It caps every problem at a single reasoning step
It translates the latent vectors back into readable text

flashcards.explanation_html: The stopping head gives the model an adaptive way to decide when to stop, so RL can allocate longer latent computation to harder instances.
